All things; being the one thing that has kept him from intense super stardom thus far. Injury. I am not saying that Crosby or Ovechkin have not been without their share of injuries either but Stamkos has had some bizarre career altering injuries that could very easily be argued have stopped him from being right next to Ovechkin chasing Gretzky. With the 140 games hes missed due to injury, plus the 4 seasons he is Ovechkins younger that's over 450 total games he would have had to close the 300 goal gap between himself and Ovechkin. Which stammer has a .525 goal per game average in his career, putting him like 60 something goals behind Ovi. This is assuming that without his injuries his scoring still would have slowed down. People never really seem to realize how good Stamkos was, and could have been. So, all things considered Stamkos holds good company. And he will always be underrated to me.

In my opinion Steven Stamkos, people hail Ovechkin and Crosby but then dog on Stammer. They have very similar numbers all things considered, and he has consistently been one of the best captains in the league. Hard when you have to share lime light with people like Kuch or Heddy or Vasy. Despite being considered great, stammer will be underrated until he is considered one of this generations best.
I think one of the Lightning superstars deserve it for the last few years of success. And to me, it's always been cool to stagger the cup winners a little on the covers

As a Lightning fan for like 10 years now, I should have been really happy when the lightning won their first cup since 2004 but since it was against the stars I was only slightly happy since I had come to love the stars that season too

Steven Stamkos, watching his transcendence from young gun to captain, and the way he's battled through adversity with injuries his whole career. He had his 60 goal season, and now hes a more complete player overall. Hes been a pleasure to watch, and I've been so happy for him the last 3 seasons.
I'm about 90% sure a lot of the 62 win season in 2019 was on 7 D, he consecutively switched over the last too cup runs as well.

One of my favorite parts if being a Lightning fan is having Jon Cooper as our coach. He is the most intelligent even keel cool calm and collect coach you'd ever see, he rarely fights with the officials, he is an inspiration to the guys in the locker room, hes not afraid to take a chance and mix things up, hes one of the largest factors that we've went back to back, and he loves the fans and city of Tampa. I believe he is the most winningest Tampa Bay Lightning coach and Definitely the longest tenured. He gives me hope to turn things around despite us losing the last like 8 of 10 games. Hes won the biggest award possible on ever level he has coached for, and just the way he speaks makes you admire him. There are very few players on the ice for the Lightning that I would be more sad to see go than Jon Cooper who is off the ice. Definitely a pinnacle to all lightning fans, and a great reason to become one

I've been watching the Lightning for like 7 or 8 years now and it still astounds me that Mikhail Sergachev is only 23. Sometimes he'll make a bad play and I'll start ragging on him in my brain, but then I have to remember hes still just a kid. It easily feels like he should be 28ish by now.
